test_title: PYST 53: SSC CGL 2024 - English (Held On 11 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law / attended the meeting / as his health is not more good.

options.text: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law
as his health is not more good

solution:
The correct answer is 4 i.e. this part of the sentence contains a grammatical error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "his health is not more good" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be "their health is not good anymore" or "their health is no longer good".

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law attended the meeting as their health is not good anymore.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "More good" is incorrect; "better" should be used for comparisons, or expressions like "not good anymore" should be used to indicate a negative change in state.
 
• When talking about health deterioration, "not good anymore" indicates the current state effectively.
